questions.def: Inversion is required after negative adverbs like 'never'.
questions.question: Never ___ I seen such a beautiful sunset.

questions.def: Adverbs modify verbs. 'Carefully' is the adverb.
questions.question: She placed the vase ___ on the table.

questions.def: 'Seldom' is the correct adverb to use for inversion.
questions.question: ___ do we see such dedication.

questions.def: Adverbs of manner (clearly) go before the verb if no object.
questions.question: The manager ___ explained the new policy to the staff.

questions.def: Inversion is required after 'hardly' at the start of a clause.
questions.question: Hardly ___ left the house when it started raining.

questions.def: 'Often' is the correct adverb to ask about frequency.
questions.question: How ___ do you visit your family?

questions.def: Inversion is required after 'little' when it starts a clause.
questions.question: Little ___ he know what was coming.

questions.def: Adverbs of time (immediately) often go at the end.
questions.question: The report needs to be completed ___.

questions.def: 'Rarely' requires inversion.
questions.question: ___ does she go to the cinema.

questions.def: Inversion follows 'scarcely': auxiliary verb then subject.
questions.question: Scarcely ___ he arrived when the phone rang.

questions.def: Adverbs of manner go after the verb if there's no object.
questions.question: The audience applauded ___ after the performance.

questions.def: 'Only then' requires inversion.
questions.question: ___ then did I understand the truth.

questions.def: Adverbs of frequency usually go before main verb.
questions.question: She ___ goes to the gym on weekends.

questions.def: Use 'more' + adverb to form comparative for adverbs.
questions.question: He sings ___ than his brother.

questions.def: 'Well' is the adverbial form of 'good'.
questions.question: She speaks English ___.

questions.def: Adverbs of manner often go after the verb + object.
questions.question: The children ___ ate their dinner.

questions.def: Adverb of manner to describe how he drove.
questions.question: He drove ___ to the airport.

questions.def: 'Badly' is the adverbial form of 'bad'.
questions.question: He performed ___ in the competition.

questions.def: 'No sooner...than' is a common structure with inversion.
questions.question: ___ had I sat down than the phone rang.

questions.def: Adverb of manner to describe how she danced.
questions.question: She danced ___ at the party.

questions.def: 'Loudly' is the adverb, describing how the music played.
questions.question: The music played ___.

questions.def: Inversion is required after 'not only' at the start.
questions.question: Not only ___ she beautiful, but also intelligent.

questions.def: Adverb 'perfectly' modifies the verb 'understood'.
questions.question: He ___ understood the instructions.

questions.def: Inversion after 'only after' requires auxiliary verb before the subject.
questions.question: Only after the meeting ___ I realize the problem.

questions.def: Inversion with 'never' requires auxiliary verb before the subject.
questions.question: Never ___ such a beautiful sunset.

questions.def: 'Hardly' requires inversion: 'Hardly had I'.
questions.question: Hardly I had entered the room when it started.

questions.def: 'Seldom' requires inversion: 'Seldom do we'.
questions.question: ___ do we experience such kindness.

questions.def: 'So + adjective' is followed by 'that' to express a result.
questions.question: So delicious was the cake ___ I ate two slices.

questions.def: 'Not only...but also' requires inversion in the first clause only.
questions.question: Not only is he intelligent, ___ also very kind.

questions.def: Adverbs should be used with verbs: 'precisely'.
questions.question: She spoke clearly and precise about the plan.
